clue.text: After disturbance, centre court's crowd finally gets composed again

indicators.note: once disturbed, the letters of the tennis venue's name are thrown into a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word crowd

explanation.surface: A Wimbledon crowd, after some disruption on Centre Court, finally settles down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After disturbance' shuffles CENTRECOURTS with D, the last letter of 'crowd' ('finally').
explanation.definitionFit: Something rebuilt or put together a second time has been reassembled, a synonym phrase for composed again.

clue.text: No longer taking exercise, one in depression needed to get fit

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: in puts the letter for one inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former fitness fanatic, now in a slump, needs to get back in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is not physical fitness but suitability.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means suitable or advantageous for a purpose, so appropriate in the sense of fit.

clue.text: Conspirator established a ring for revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: set means established, as in set up
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A plotter set up a cell to bring about an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for revolution' reverses SETAO. Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot of 1678.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates fabricated a Catholic plot against Charles II, making him a notorious plotter.

clue.text: King, consumed by evils, becomes understood

indicators.note: being consumed by something means being swallowed inside it

parts.note: two evils, sin and sin
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is swallowed up by his vices, and his nature is finally grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'evils' gives two SINs, with K between them.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea finally sinks in, it is absorbed and grasped by the mind.

clue.text: Might he be cruelly construed as Darwin's arch kid?

definitions.text: Might he be cruelly construed as Darwin's arch kid?

indicators.note: construed cruelly, the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Is this scientist, perhaps unkindly, being cast as Darwin's mischievous offspring?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly construed' rearranges DARWINSARCHKID; the whole clue also describes the man.
explanation.definitionFit: The evolutionary biologist is Darwin's best-known modern champion, an intellectual heir and arch admirer.

clue.text: Story of church fellow in charge, having drink, losing head

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, any fellow
IC means in charge

indicators.note: losing its head drops the first letter of the word for drink

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A tale of a churchman in charge who takes to drink and loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts ALE to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical account of events in order, a story or record.

clue.text: English spirit? Little left in a Scottish place

indicators.note: in puts the small letter for left inside English spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit
L is the abbreviation for left, and lower-case is little

explanation.surface: An English gin with a drop left over, found in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in Moray in north-east Scotland, a place name.

clue.text: Unnamed items, poor devices getting sticky inside

parts.note: thin can mean poor or meagre
gummy means sticky
jigs are devices that guide tools

explanation.surface: Nameless gadgets, poorly made, get gunked up inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingummyjig is a placeholder word for an object whose name escapes you, so these are unnamed things.

clue.text: Style me angrier type in religious get-together

indicators.note: to style is to fashion or arrange, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross person urges a stylist to make them angrier at a church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' rearranges MEANGRIERTYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of believers held for worship and communal intercession is a church get-together.

clue.text: Fixer to note: this is lacking muscle tone

parts.note: hypo is sodium thiosulphate, the fixer used in developing photographs
the tonic is the keynote of a musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone who fixes things is told to note that this is a weak, slack condition.
explanation.walkthrough: HYPO is old darkroom slang for photographic fixing solution; 'to' and 'this is' simply join the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine the term describes muscles with abnormally low tension, so it means lacking normal tone.

clue.text: Prank on the Queen makes one very cross

parts.note: a rag is a student prank or practical joke
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A practical joke played on the monarch leaves her furious.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a fury, raging with temper, is one who is very cross; an informal noun from the verb rage.

clue.text: Nest I had established in student organisation

indicators.note: something established in a body is placed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
I had contracts to I'd, giving ID

explanation.surface: A student society's base becomes a nest someone has set up within it.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A nidus is a nest or breeding place, especially for insects or bacteria; a Latin-derived synonym.

clue.text: Only for blokes, girl shows sluggishness

parts.note: a stag party or night is men only
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl shows little energy at an event restricted to men.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag night is a British all-male party for a man about to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnancy is the state of being still and inactive, like stagnant water, hence sluggishness.

clue.text: After meal, left university to tidy up

parts.note: to neaten is to tidy up

explanation.surface: After eating, someone departs the college to clean the place up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After meal' and 'left' look like separate instructions, but together they define food left on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Food not consumed is what remains on the plate when the meal is over.

clue.text: Irish chief's philosophical principle one gets to see through, not right

parts.note: the Tao is the guiding principle of Taoist philosophy
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: to search is to look right through something

explanation.surface: The Irish leader's guiding philosophy is something one comes to see through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' drops R from SEARCH; 'gets to' is link and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of the Republic of Ireland, its head of government.

clue.text: Editor turning to drink, one with last word?

indicators.note: turning means the two letters for editor are read the other way round

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor takes to drink, yet still insists on having the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses ED to DE, and 'to' simply joins it to CIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever settles a matter, or a deciding game, has the final say; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: System of reasoning set up has frantic hospital missing out

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: laid means set down

indicators.note: missing out means the hospital's letter is dropped

parts.note: hectic means frantic

explanation.surface: A setup in which a frantic hospital leaves something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses LAID to DIAL; 'missing out' removes H from HECTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is a method of argument through thesis and counter-thesis, a philosophical reasoning system.

clue.text: More than one saw some tot misbehaving

indicators.note: a misbehaving group is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watched a few toddlers behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a past tense verb, but here it is a noun meaning a saying; 'misbehaving' rearranges SOMETOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, so several sayings of that kind are maxims or watchwords.

clue.text: Musical passage starts to sound terrific, really exciting to the audience

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A piece of music begins sounding terrific and thrills the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretta is a closing section of an opera or fugue played at a faster tempo, a musical passage.

clue.text: End of term, when book's to be returned?

definitions.meaning: the expected date of birth at the end of a pregnancy's term
the date by which a library loan must go back

explanation.surface: A student wonders when the library books must go back as the school term closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' suggests a school term, but here it is the full length of a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the predicted day of a baby's arrival and a library's deadline for return.

clue.text: See 5
Revolting man, who's a bit of a game

definitions.meaning: ... was a leader in the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
one of the thin sticks in the game of spillikins

explanation.surface: A disgusting fellow who is something of a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting: the man led the English Peasants' Revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebel's name is also the word for a single stick in pick-up-sticks, so a game piece.

clue.text: Endless manure thrown over home plant

indicators.note: thrown over means turned the other way, read backwards
endless removes the final letter from the word for manure

parts.note: muck is manure
in means at home

explanation.surface: Manure spread over a plant at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts MUCK to MUC, and 'thrown over' reverses it to CUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is an aromatic herb of the parsley family, grown for its seeds.

clue.text: Corn — that which is full of energy?

indicators.note: a container full of something holds it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: what can mean that which, as in 'what I need'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a corn variety that is supposedly packed with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use corn often means wheat or grain generally, not maize.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is a general British term for cereal grain, and this grain is the commonest example.

clue.text: Sort of bird to deviate, missing north

indicators.note: missing means the letter for north is absent from the word

parts.note: to wander is to stray or deviate

explanation.surface: A bird that strays from course and fails to head north.
explanation.definitionFit: Waders are long-legged shore birds such as herons and sandpipers, a category of bird.

clue.text: Graduate school first to get low grade

indicators.note: first says the school's letters come at the front, ahead of the graduate

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate school's first student gets a poor mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a pod of whales, GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The third letter of the Greek alphabet is used for a third-class mark, a poor exam result.

clue.text: Sea god, grabbing English princess, attempted seduction

indicators.note: the sea god grabbing something holds it inside his name

parts.note: Triton is the Greek sea god, son of Poseidon
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A sea god seizes an English princess and tries to seduce her.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is British slang for making a sexual advance or chancing one's luck.

clue.text: Where a summary may be found, theoretically

definitions.text: Where a summary may be found
definitions.meaning: a summary of a paper sits in its abstract
considered in general terms, not concretely

explanation.surface: An academic notes that, in theory, the summary lives at the top of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places something within a paper's summary, and idiomatically means in general or theoretical terms.
